chunks: And regarding the cheek, if there is a perforation in it from which the inside of the mouth can be seen, its wergild is two hundred dinars; and if it was treated, healed, and united, and there is a clear mark and a prominent scar upon it, its wergild is fifty dinars. So if the perforation was in both cheeks, its wergild is one hundred dinars, and that is half the wergild of that from which the mouth is seen.

So if it was a strike with a blade that embeds in the bone to the extent that it pierces to the jaw, its wergild is one hundred and fifty dinars, fifty of which are assigned for exposing the bone; and if it was a perforation and did not pierce into it, its wergild is one hundred dinars. So if it has a scar, the wergild for its scar is in addition to the wergild for exposing the bone.

So if it was a wound and did not expose (bone), then it healed and was in the two cheeks, its wergild is ten dinars. So if it was in the face as a fracture, its wergild is eighty dinars. So if a piece of flesh fell from it and it did not expose (bone), and it was the size of a dirham or more, its wergild is thirty dinars. And the wergild of the strike when it exposes (bone) is forty dinars when it is in the cheek.

And regarding the exposing of the bone in the head, it is fifty dinars. So if the bones were displaced from it, its wergild is one hundred and fifty dinars. So if it was a perforation in the head, that is the Al-Ma'mumah, its wergild is three hundred and thirty-three dinars and one-third of a dinar.

key_terms.الْمَأْمُومَة: A specific type of skull fracture reaching the brain
key_terms.دَنَانِير: Gold dinars, a unit of currency
key_terms.شَيْن: Scar or mark left after healing
key_terms.صَدْع: Fracture or crack in the bone
key_terms.مُوضِحَة: Exposure of the bone beneath the skin
key_terms.نَافِذَة: A perforation or hole through which something can be seen

ai.seo_question: What is the blood money (diyah) for a facial injury that exposes the bone or causes a skull fracture?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* elaborates on the jurisprudence of *diyah* (blood money) for facial injuries, specifically addressing the *khad* (cheek) and head, with distinctions based on depth, bone exposure, and scarring. It reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of categorizing injuries by their permanence and severity, such as differentiating between *mudhiha* (bone-exposing) and *naqiba* (deep) wounds. The text provides a detailed legal framework for compensating specific anatomical damages, underscoring the precision required in Islamic inheritance and compensation law.

en.hubeali: And regarding the cheek, when there is a rupture in it from which the inside of the mouth can be seen, so its wergild is two hundred Dinars; and if medication is applied so it is cured, and complete, and due to it there is a clear mark and an obscene tear, so its wergild is fifty Dinars. So if there was piercing in both of the cheeks, so its wergild is one hundred Dinars. And that is half the wergild of that from which the (inside of) the mouth can be seen.

So if it had been jabbed at with a blade which affirmed into the bone to the extent that it pierced into the jaw, so its wergild is one hundred and fifty Dinars, fifty of which have been made to be for exposing it (the bone); and if it had caused a blister and did not get affirmed in it, so its wergild is one hundred Dinars; so if it had exposed something from the face, so its wergild would be fifty Dinars; so if it was that it had ugliness for it, so its wergild would be for it along with the wergild for the exposure (of the bone).

So if it has been a wound and did not expose (a bone), then it was cured, and it was in the two cheeks, so its wergild would be ten Dinars; so if it was in the face as a fracture, its wergild would be eighty Dinars; so if a piece of the flesh had fallen from it, and it did not expose bone), and it was the size of the Dirham, and it was not above that, its wergild would be thirty Dinars; and a wergild of the piercing when it had exposed (the bone) is forty Dinars, when it was in the cheek.

And with regards to exposure (of the bone) in the head, it is fifty Dinars; so if the bone had been displaced from it, its wergild is one hundred and fifty Dinars. So if it had been pierced in the head, so that would be Al-Mamouma (the skull fracture reaching the brain), its wergild is three hundred and thirty three Dinars and one-third of a Dinar.
